To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
6 sheep fed individually in metabolic cages for 7 days are required to measure dry matter digestibility of perennial ryegrass and forage rape to a precision of ±5 g/kg DM.

1) The number of sheep needed to achieve an acceptable level of precision for DM digestibility of fresh perennial ryegrasses or forage rape, when sheep are already acclimatising to these diets, is 6 sheep fed individually for 4 days followed by 7 d measurement, and 2) If sheep are not used to fresh forages, then 8 sheep should be used and the measurement period increased to 11 days.
the precision of digestible organic matter (DOMD) estimates is affected by both the number of sheep used in a trial and the length of the trial.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a protocol to measure the DM digestibility of sheep when fed fresh perennial grasses or forages.

the development of a protocol for digestibility trials using fresh forage, with the objective of reducing the variation between animals, and therefore the required number of animals, in digestibility trials.
the development of a protocol for digestibility trials with fresh perennial ryegrasses and forage rape, which are commonly grazed by sheep and cattle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
6 animals are required to achieve the desired standard errors of 5 g/kg, and that a 4-day acclimatisation period followed by 7-day measurements is required.

the precision of the digestibility estimate is improved by increasing the number of sheep, increasing the length of acclimatisation period, and increasing the duration of the measurement period, with the greatest effect on precision being achieved by increasing the number and length of the acclimatisa-tion period.

a minimum of 4 sheep should be used for digestibility trials of fresh perennial ryegrasses or forage raps if the acclimatisation period is 4 days and the measurement period 7 days, and that 6 sheep should be used if the acclimation is 4 days followed by 7 d of measurement, or if acclimation is not used and 7 d of individual measurements are made.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sheep numbers required for digestibility evaluations with these feeds are similar to those used for other feeds.

if sheep are acclimatising to a fresh perennial rye grass or forage rape feed, and if the standard error is equal to or greater than 4 g/kg, then a minimum number of 8 sheep should be used and 7 days of measurements.

if a digestibility trial is required with fresh perennial ryegrasses or forage rapes, the number of animals needed is dependent on the level of precision required for the estimate, and the duration for which the animals are acclimatising to the diet and the duration of the measurement period.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the precision of the digestibility estimate is more important than the number of animals, and that the precision is improved by increasing the measurement period duration, or increasing the number of sheep, or both.
the precision of digestible organic matter (DOM) digestibility estimates can be improved by increasing the duration of acclimatising the sheep to the feed and by increasing the number of animals.
the precision of digestible organic matter (DOMD) can be improved by increasing the number of sheep and/or the duration of the measurement period.
